filesystemLocations.label: User Documents

filesystemLocations.label: User Downloads
filesystemLocations.description: All files and subdirectories inside the user's Downloads folder

filesystemLocations.label: User Desktop
filesystemLocations.description: All files and subdirectories on the user's Desktop

filesystemLocations.label: SSH Keys & Config
filesystemLocations.description: SSH private keys, public keys, and config files used for remote server access

filesystemLocations.label: Cloud Credentials (AWS)
filesystemLocations.description: AWS access keys, secret keys, and session tokens used for cloud infrastructure access

filesystemLocations.label: Kubernetes Config
filesystemLocations.description: Kubernetes cluster credentials and configuration - grants access to container orchestration

filesystemLocations.label: Environment Files
filesystemLocations.description: Files like .env, .env.local, .env.production, prod.env - often contain API keys, database passwords, and secrets

filesystemLocations.label: GPG Keys
filesystemLocations.description: GPG encryption keys used for signing commits, encrypting files, and verifying identities

filesystemLocations.label: System Configuration
filesystemLocations.description: OS-level configuration files (hosts, DNS, PAM, cron, etc.) - modifying these can affect system behavior

filesystemLocations.label: System Binaries
filesystemLocations.description: Core OS executables - writing here could replace system commands with malicious ones

filesystemLocations.label: System Libraries
filesystemLocations.description: Shared libraries used by the OS and applications - tampering can break or backdoor software

filesystemLocations.label: Temporary Files
filesystemLocations.description: Temporary file storage - agents may use /tmp to stage payloads or exfiltrate data

filesystemLocations.label: Entire Home Directory
filesystemLocations.description: Everything inside the user's home directory including documents, configs, and secrets

filesystemLocations.label: All Paths (catch-all)
filesystemLocations.description: Matches every filesystem path - use as a default rule at the end of a policy

network.label: AI/LLM APIs

network.label: Model Hubs
network.description: Platforms for downloading and running open-source ML models - agents may pull model weights or run inference

network.label: Code Repositories
network.description: Source code hosting - agents may clone repos, push code changes, or access private repositories

network.label: Package Registries
network.description: Package managers where agents install dependencies - risk of pulling malicious or vulnerable packages

network.label: Container Registries
network.description: Container image registries - agents may pull or push Docker images that run arbitrary code

network.label: CI/CD Platforms
network.description: Continuous integration and deployment services - agents interacting here could trigger builds or deployments

network.label: AWS Services
network.description: Amazon Web Services APIs (S3, EC2, Lambda, IAM, etc.) - broad cloud infrastructure access

network.label: GCP Services
network.description: Google Cloud Platform APIs - compute, storage, AI, and other cloud services

network.label: Azure Services
network.description: Microsoft Azure cloud services - VMs, databases, identity, and other infrastructure

network.label: Monitoring & Observability
network.description: Monitoring tools - agents may read sensitive metrics/logs or trigger incident alerts

network.label: Cloud Instance Metadata (IMDS)
network.description: Instance metadata endpoints on AWS, GCP, and Azure - a request here hands back the machine's cloud credentials

network.label: Slack
network.description: Slack messaging platform - agents may read messages, send messages, or access shared files

network.label: Atlassian (Jira/Confluence)
network.description: Jira and Confluence - agents may access project tickets, wiki pages, and internal documentation

network.label: Notion
network.description: Notion workspace - agents may read/write pages, databases, and shared team knowledge

network.label: Google Workspace
network.description: Google Workspace (Drive, Docs, Sheets, Gmail) - broad access to documents and email

network.label: Linear
network.description: Linear project management - agents may read/create issues and access project data

network.label: File Sharing
network.description: File sharing and one-shot upload services - high risk for data exfiltration if an agent uploads sensitive files

network.label: Paste & Snippet Sites
network.description: Public paste/snippet sites - agents could leak source code, secrets, or internal data

network.label: Tunnels & Request Inspectors
network.description: Tunnel and request-inspection endpoints - an agent can post data to one from anywhere, or expose a local service to the internet

network.label: Personal Email
network.description: Personal email providers - risk of agents sending sensitive data to external addresses

network.label: Social Media
network.description: Social media platforms - agents could post internal information publicly

network.label: All External Traffic
network.description: Matches all network destinations - use as a catch-all default rule at the end of a policy

network.label: Internal Network
network.description: Private/internal network ranges only - restricts agents to on-premise or VPN resources

credentials.label: SSH Private Keys
credentials.description: Private key files (id_rsa, id_ed25519, etc.) used to authenticate to remote servers

credentials.label: SSH Directory
credentials.description: Entire SSH directory including keys, config, and known hosts

credentials.label: SSH Known Hosts
credentials.description: List of previously connected servers - modifying could enable man-in-the-middle attacks

credentials.label: AWS Credentials
credentials.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key - grants programmatic access to AWS services

credentials.label: AWS Config
credentials.description: AWS CLI configuration including default region, output format, and SSO settings

credentials.label: GCP Service Accounts
credentials.description: Google Cloud service account keys and CLI credentials

credentials.label: Azure Credentials
credentials.description: Azure CLI tokens and subscription credentials

credentials.label: Kubernetes Config
credentials.description: Cluster connection details and auth tokens - grants access to manage Kubernetes resources

credentials.label: Docker Config
credentials.description: Docker registry auth tokens - allows pulling/pushing container images

credentials.label: Terraform Credentials
credentials.description: Terraform Cloud/Enterprise API tokens - grants access to infrastructure-as-code state

credentials.label: Environment Files (.env)
credentials.description: Dotenv files containing API keys, database URLs, and other application secrets

credentials.label: GPG Keys
credentials.description: GPG encryption and signing keys - used for commit signing and file encryption

credentials.label: Keychain / Secret Store
credentials.description: OS-level credential stores (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager and DPAPI vaults) containing saved passwords and tokens

credentials.label: NPM Tokens
credentials.description: NPM registry authentication tokens - can be used to publish packages under your identity

credentials.label: Git Credentials
credentials.description: Stored Git usernames and passwords/tokens for repository access

credentials.label: Process Environment (/proc)
credentials.description: Linux process environment blocks - reading these lifts tokens straight out of a running process

credentials.label: Database & Storage Client Credentials
credentials.description: Postgres, MySQL, Google Cloud Storage, and S3 client config files - each stores its password or access key in plaintext

credentials.label: Password Manager Vaults
credentials.description: KeePass-family vault files - one file holding every password the user saved

credentials.label: All Credential Locations
credentials.description: All known credential file locations combined - broadest credential access rule

capabilities.label: Shell / Terminal - Any command
capabilities.description: Matches every shell command (bash, zsh, sh, cmd.exe, PowerShell). Most powerful capability - allows arbitrary system access. Use sparingly.

capabilities.label: Code interpreters (python, node, PowerShell, …)
capabilities.description: Running code via interpreters (Python, Node.js, PowerShell Invoke-Expression, cmd /c, .ps1 scripts) - can execute arbitrary logic. Narrower than process_spawn (which also covers non-interpreter spawn vectors like mshta, rundll32, Start-Process).

capabilities.label: Process - Meta-execution only (eval, bash -c)
capabilities.description: Matches `eval`, `exec`, and `bash/sh/zsh -c "..."` - meta-execution patterns that hide the real command from static rules. Highest-risk subset of process spawning.

capabilities.label: Process spawning - Any (nohup, exec, Start-Process, mshta, rundll32, …)
capabilities.description: Launching new OS processes (nohup, exec, Start-Process, rundll32, mshta, wmic, cmd /c, powershell -Command). Broader than the meta-execution variant.

capabilities.label: Privileged execution (sudo, runas, gsudo)
capabilities.description: Running commands with elevated privileges - sudo on Unix, runas / gsudo / psexec / Start-Process -Verb RunAs / -RunAs flag on Windows. Full system control if allowed.

capabilities.label: File read (any path)
capabilities.description: Reading file contents from disk - agents may access source code, configs, or sensitive data.

capabilities.label: File write / create (any path)
capabilities.description: Creating or modifying files - agents can change code, configs, or install scripts.

capabilities.label: File delete (rm, del, Remove-Item)
capabilities.description: Matches `rm`, `del`, `erase`, `rd`, `rmdir`, `Remove-Item`, `Clear-RecycleBin`. Irreversible data loss if misused.

capabilities.label: Permissions - Unsafe only (setuid, 777, 666)
capabilities.description: Matches dangerous chmod patterns (setuid/setgid bits, world-writable). Narrower than the all-chmod preset.

capabilities.label: Permissions - Any (chmod, chown, icacls, attrib, …)
capabilities.description: Matches chmod/chown/chgrp on Unix and icacls/attrib/takeown/Set-Acl/Get-Acl on Windows. Broader than the unsafe-only variant.

capabilities.label: File Copy / Move (cp, mv, copy, robocopy, Copy-Item)
capabilities.description: Copying, moving, or linking files (cp, mv, ln, copy, xcopy, robocopy, move, mklink, Copy-Item, Move-Item, Rename-Item) - data-staging / exfiltration vector symmetric across Unix and Windows.

capabilities.label: Drive-by execution (`curl … | bash`)
capabilities.description: Matches `curl ... | bash` and `wget ... | sh` patterns specifically - the classic drive-by RCE vector.

capabilities.label: Web - Outbound write only (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE, --data, --upload-file)
capabilities.description: Matches HTTP requests that send data out - POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE methods, `--data`, `-F`, `--upload-file`, `-T`. The exfil/mutation pattern; GET-style fetches stay under the broad web_access preset.

capabilities.label: Web / HTTP - Any (curl, wget, Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin)
capabilities.description: Matches every HTTP/HTTPS client invocation - curl, wget, http, fetch, Invoke-WebRequest, iwr, irm, Start-BitsTransfer, certutil -urlcache, bitsadmin /transfer. Broader than the outbound-write and curl-to-shell variants.

capabilities.label: DNS lookups (dig, nslookup, Resolve-DnsName)
capabilities.description: Resolving domain names - dig, nslookup, host, resolvectl, Resolve-DnsName. Can be used for DNS tunneling or reconnaissance.

capabilities.label: Socket - Listen / bind only (nc -l, socat …LISTEN:)
capabilities.description: Matches socket-listening commands that open this endpoint to inbound connections. Subset of socket_open; outbound `nc <host>`, `nmap`, and `telnet` stay under the broad preset.

capabilities.label: Raw socket / port access - Any (nc, socat, nmap, Test-NetConnection, …)
capabilities.description: Opening raw TCP/UDP sockets (nc, netcat, socat, nmap, telnet, Test-NetConnection, [System.Net.Sockets]). Broader than the listen/bind variant.

capabilities.label: Git - Outbound only (push)
capabilities.description: Matches `git push` and `git send-pack` - operations that send data to the remote and affect other team members.

capabilities.label: Git - Inbound only (pull, fetch, clone)
capabilities.description: Matches `git pull`, `git fetch`, `git clone` - operations that pull data into this endpoint.

capabilities.label: Git - Any remote op (push + pull + fetch + clone)
capabilities.description: Matches any git operation that touches a remote. Coarser than the outbound/inbound split.

capabilities.label: Git - Destructive only (force push, hard reset, filter-branch)
capabilities.description: Matches force pushes, hard resets, and history-rewriting commands.

capabilities.label: Git - Any command
capabilities.description: Matches every git subcommand including read-only ones. Broader than the variants above.

capabilities.label: Docker - Outbound only (push)
capabilities.description: Matches `docker push` / `podman push` - pushes an image to the registry.

capabilities.label: Docker - Inbound only (pull)
capabilities.description: Matches `docker pull` / `podman pull` - pulls an image to this endpoint.

capabilities.label: Docker - Any registry op (push + pull)
capabilities.description: Matches any docker/podman push or pull. Coarser than the outbound/inbound split.

capabilities.label: Docker - Destructive only (rm, prune, volume rm)
capabilities.description: Matches container/image/volume removal. Read-only ops like `docker ps` and `docker logs` pass through.

capabilities.label: Docker - Any command
capabilities.description: Matches every docker/podman subcommand. Broader than the variants above.

capabilities.label: Kubernetes - Destructive only (delete, drain, scale-to-zero)
capabilities.description: Matches destructive cluster ops only. Subset of the broader mutate preset.

capabilities.label: Kubernetes - Any mutation (apply, create, patch, delete, …)
capabilities.description: Matches any kubectl command that mutates the cluster (apply/create/patch/replace/edit/scale/delete/drain/cordon). Read-only ops pass through.

capabilities.label: Kubernetes - Secret reads only
capabilities.description: Matches `kubectl get secret`, `externalsecret`, and `secretstore` - for cluster secret exfiltration.

capabilities.label: Kubernetes - Any command
capabilities.description: Matches every kubectl/helm/k9s/oc invocation. Broader than the variants above.

capabilities.label: AWS CLI - Secret / credential reads
capabilities.description: Matches `aws secretsmanager get-secret-value`, `list-secrets`, and `ssm get-parameter --with-decryption` - for AWS secret exfiltration.

capabilities.label: AWS CLI - Any command
capabilities.description: Matches every `aws` CLI invocation. Broader than the secret-reads variant above.

capabilities.label: HashiCorp Vault - Secret reads
capabilities.description: Matches `vault read` and `vault kv get` - pulls secret material out of a Vault server. Listing and status commands pass through.

capabilities.label: 1Password CLI - Secret reads
capabilities.description: Matches `op item get` and `op read` - pulls an item or a secret reference out of a 1Password vault.

capabilities.label: Google Cloud - Secret Manager reads
capabilities.description: Matches `gcloud secrets versions access` - reads a secret's value out of Google Secret Manager. `gcloud secrets list` passes through.

capabilities.label: Akeyless - Secret reads
capabilities.description: Matches `akeyless get-secret-value` and `akeyless get-secret` - pulls secret material out of Akeyless.

capabilities.label: Terraform - Destructive only (destroy, apply -destroy)
capabilities.description: Matches `terraform destroy` / `tofu destroy` and `apply -destroy` - tears down managed infrastructure. `plan` and read-only commands pass through.

capabilities.label: Package - Publish only (npm/yarn/pnpm/cargo/gem/twine)
capabilities.description: Matches `npm publish`, `yarn publish`, `cargo publish`, `gem publish`, `twine upload`, etc. - package publication to a registry, which affects everyone who installs your package.

capabilities.label: Package install - Global only (`npm i -g`, `pip --user`, `brew install`)
capabilities.description: Matches global / system-wide installs only. Project-local installs pass through.

capabilities.label: Package install - Any (npm, pip, winget, choco, scoop, …)
capabilities.description: Matches every package-manager install invocation - Unix (npm/pip/gem/cargo/brew/apt/yarn/pnpm/bun) plus Windows (winget, choco, scoop, msiexec /i, Install-Module, Install-Package). Broader than global-only.

capabilities.label: Package manager - Any command
capabilities.description: Matches any npm/yarn/pnpm/bun/pip/gem/cargo/brew/apt/twine invocation. Broader than the install + publish variants.

capabilities.label: Clipboard - Read only (pbpaste, xclip -o, wl-paste)
capabilities.description: Matches commands that READ the clipboard - the actual exfil pattern that captures passwords/tokens an operator just copied. Subset of clipboard_access; pbcopy/xclip -i/wl-copy stay under the broad preset.

capabilities.label: Clipboard - Any (pbcopy, xclip, clip, Get-Clipboard, …)
capabilities.description: Reading or writing the system clipboard - pbcopy, pbpaste, xclip, xsel, wl-copy, wl-paste, clip.exe, Get-Clipboard, Set-Clipboard. Broader than the read-only variant.

capabilities.label: Screenshot / screen capture (screencapture, scrot, SnippingTool)
capabilities.description: Taking screenshots of the display - screencapture (macOS), scrot/gnome-screenshot/flameshot (Linux), SnippingTool.exe and [System.Drawing.Graphics]::CopyFromScreen (Windows). Can capture any visible sensitive information.

capabilities.label: Environment variable access (env, $env:, setx, …)
capabilities.description: Reading environment variables - env/printenv/export/source on Unix, setx/$env:/[Environment]::/reg query Environment/ls env: on Windows. Often contain API keys, tokens, and connection strings.

capabilities.label: Environment variable dump (env, printenv, Get-ChildItem env:)
capabilities.description: Dumping the complete process environment, which commonly exposes API keys, tokens, and connection strings.

capabilities.label: Browser automation (puppeteer, playwright, …)
capabilities.description: Controlling a web browser programmatically - can interact with authenticated web sessions.

capabilities.label: Modify Windows Registry
capabilities.description: Modifying Windows registry via reg.exe add/delete, regini, Set-ItemProperty, or New-ItemProperty - persistence and config tampering vector.

capabilities.label: Windows Service Control
capabilities.description: Creating, starting, stopping, or deleting Windows services (sc.exe, net start/stop, New-Service, Start-Service, Stop-Service) - persistence and privilege-escalation vector.

capabilities.label: Windows Scheduled Tasks
capabilities.description: Creating or modifying Windows scheduled tasks (schtasks.exe with create/change/delete/run/end verbs, at.exe, Register-ScheduledTask) - persistence vector similar to Unix cron. Read-only `schtasks /query` does not match.

capabilities.label: Modify Windows Firewall
capabilities.description: Adding, removing, or disabling Windows firewall rules (netsh advfirewall, New-NetFirewallRule, Set-NetFirewallRule) - defense-evasion and lateral-movement enabler.

capabilities.label: All capabilities (catch-all)
capabilities.description: Matches every capability - use as a catch-all default rule at the end of a policy.

mcp.label: Workflow automation
